laat_vaar.blok: Waarom 'n ketel meer vra as 'n radio
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: As a multiplier the plural 'kere' is the standard form, and 'baie keer' also reads as 'often', which blurs the comparison.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'baie keer groter' is standard, natural Afrikaans (like 'twee keer groter') and cannot be read as 'often' after a number comparison, so 'kere' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: niks daarmee te doen gehad het nie
laat_vaar.na: niks daarmee te doen het nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The rest of the sentence is in the present tense, so the past perfect is out of step; the present tense keeps the meaning (a child who is not involved) and reads more naturally.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The past perfect is correct: it says the child had no part in making the connection, which happened earlier; the present tense blurs that and the original reads naturally.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoe lank dit aan is, tel ook
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die meeste van Suid-Afrika se elektrisiteit
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die grootste deel van Suid-Afrika se elektrisiteit
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Die meeste van' with an uncountable noun follows English 'most of'; 'die grootste deel van' is the natural Afrikaans and keeps the quantifier.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die meeste van' with a mass noun is normal Afrikaans, and swapping a quantifier is a lateral move with meaning risk.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The compound avoids the clumsy chain of two 'van' phrases; the protected opening of the sentence is untouched.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is clear, and a 24-letter compound is harder for a Grade 6 reader and risks the word-length gate.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Verkeerd gaan' is the standard idiom; 'verkeerd loop' is colloquial.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'As iets verkeerd loop' is standard Afrikaans, so the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Sê' needs an object here; 'sê dit' is the natural form and keeps the instruction unchanged.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Se dadelik vir 'n grootmens' is natural Afrikaans, and this is a safety instruction whose checked wording should stay.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Waarom 'n ketel meer vra as 'n radio
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Dit vra baie energie om iets warm te maak, veral water. Dit vra baie meer energie as om lig of klank te maak.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Om iets warm te maak, veral water, vra baie meer energie as om lig of klank te maak.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Two consecutive sentences open with the same 'Dit vra baie ... energie' frame; one sentence says the same comparison without the wooden repetition.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The repeated 'Dit vra baie energie ... Dit vra baie meer energie' is a clear two-step build for a Grade 6 reader, and the merge drops the stand-alone claim and buries 'veral water' as an aside inside a heavier comparison, so it is a lateral move that also shifts what 'veral water' attaches to.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: 'n substasie in 'n kas wat in baie strate staan
laat_vaar_vorige.na: 'n substasie in 'n kas, en sulke kaste staan in baie strate
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written, the relative clause says one box stands in many streets; splitting it keeps the protected wordings 'n substasie in 'n kas' and 'in baie strate' intact and fixes the reference (AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses).
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The generic 'n ... wat in baie strate staan' is normal Afrikaans for describing a kind of thing and no reader takes it as one box in many streets, so splitting it only adds words to a lesson already over budget.
